title: Dedicated capacity rapid triage and deployable fixes catalog
creator: Aisha Khan
description: This ticket consolidates a set of low-risk, high-impact deployable mitigations and a rapid triage checklist for dedicated capacity shortfalls caused by autoscaler latency regressions or control-plane scheduling delays. The goal is to reduce mean time to safe-state (MTTS) during capacity shortfalls to under 15 minutes and to catalog code/config artifacts that can be applied as tactical rollbacks or temporary safeguards while engineering performs root-cause work.
timeline: 2026-02-14 05:12 UTC: First elevated alerts (dedicated-pool headroom < 10%). 2026-02-14 05:25 UTC: Autoscaler control-plane exhibited >10s reconciliation latency; request queueing increased. 2026-02-14 05:40 UTC: Canary rollback of autoscaler v2 reverted to v1.9 — partial relief. 2026-02-14 06:05 UTC: Emergency throttles enabled for low-priority tenants; headroom recovered to 22%. 2026-02-14 09:30 UTC: Post-incident stabilization and incident command review initiated.
mitigation_summary: Apply short-lived configuration toggles and deploy pre-approved code hotfixes to restore headroom and keep SLAs intact while underlying controller fixes are validated. Use traffic shaping, tenant prioritization, and safe autoscaler rollbacks as primary levers. Instrument additional telemetry around reconciliation latency and KV cache pressure immediately.
immediate_fixes: Toggle: autoscaler.enable_fast_reconcile = false (immediate safe revert for control-plane latency spikes)
Rollback: revert autoscaler image from runtime-autoscaler:v2.1.0 -> runtime-autoscaler:v1.9.7 (pre-approved rollback PR ready)
Config: reduce max_batch_size on suspect pool types from 64 -> 32 to lower memory pressure during peak burst
Traffic control: apply per-tenant emergency rate limits for low-tier tenants via edge-policy override (edge-policy: emergency_throttle_2026-02-14)
Routing fallback: pin high-SLA customers to dedicated-reserve pool with separate admission control rule
Operational: increase fleet headroom buffer by immediately reserving two compute nodes per pool (k8s node pool scale-up or soft-reserve tag)
Observability: enable detailed reconciler tracing (trace-level=debug) for autoscaler components and increase reconciliation metrics retention to 72h in the incident namespace
deployable_fixes_catalog: PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7643 - autoscaler rollback orchestrator and safety checks (merge-ready)
Manifest: k8s/overrides/emergency-rate-limit-2026-02-14.yaml - edge policy to enforce tenant throttles
Script: ops/bin/allocate-reserve-nodes.sh - idempotent node reservation for dedicated pools
Playbook snippet: runbooks/dedicated/quick_ttl_rollbacks.md - approved rollback steps and communication templates
Template: alert-actions/scale-quick.json - API payload for immediate node reservation via infra-controlplane
Helm: charts/autoscaler/values-emergency.yaml - conservative defaults for reconcile interval and backoff
follow_up_actions: Short-term: instrument average and P99 autoscaler reconciliation latency and add burn-rate alerts (owner: infra-observability)
Short-term: create canary pipeline that runs autoscaler upgrade against 10% of pools with pre-flight memory + reconcile stress tests (owner: infra-ci)
Medium-term: implement graceful admission queue for dedicated pools to prioritize high-SLA tenants during headroom events (owner: serving-runtime)
Medium-term: add automatic fallback routing to compatible model-quantized variants when dedicated pool response time exceeds threshold (owner: routing)
Long-term: redesign autoscaler reconciliation loop to be non-blocking for scale decisions when KV cache pressure is high (owner: autoscaler-team)
Operational: update incident runbooks with the 'deployable fixes catalog' and run a quarterly fire drill (owner: SRE)
Postmortem: run RCA workshop and translate findings into prioritized backlog with acceptance criteria (owner: incident-lead)
Customer: prepare customer-facing incident summary and impacted tenant list for outreach (owner: customer-success)
Policy: formalize headroom SLOs per tenant tier and codify emergency throttle thresholds in the Console (owner: product-management)
decisions: Decision 2026-02-14: Hot rollback of autoscaler to v1.9.7 approved as first-line mitigation to restore reconcile latency (approved by: Aisha Khan, Marcus Li)
Decision 2026-02-15: Emergency tenant throttles will be encoded as temporary edge-policy overrides rather than binary pool offlines to preserve high-SLA traffic
Decision 2026-02-20: Increase default pool headroom target from 15% -> 25% for all dedicated pools until autoscaler rewrite lands
